name: Isabelo de los Reyes
description: Arrested following the August 1902 general strike organized by the Unión Obrera Democrática. He was prosecuted for sedition, conspiracy and related political offenses. The exact date of his discharge remains uncertain.

cases.charges: Sedition and conspiracy
cases.sentence: Arrested after the August 1902 general strike and prosecuted for sedition, conspiracy and related political offenses; his exact discharge date is uncertain and is omitted here.

name: Dominador Gómez
description: Arrested on May 1, 1903 as a labor and nationalist organizer. He received terms reported as four years plus an additional year at hard labor. He regained his freedom after assisting negotiations for Macario Sakay's surrender in 1906.

cases.charges: Labor and nationalist organizing
cases.sentence: Arrested May 1, 1903 and given terms reported as four years plus an additional year at hard labor, but regained his freedom in 1906 after assisting negotiations for Macario Sakay's surrender.

name: Aurelio Tolentino
description: Arrested on May 14, 1903 for staging the anti-colonial drama Kahapon, Ngayon at Bukas. He was released on bail in December 1903, rearrested in June 1904, and eventually paroled on February 5, 1907.

cases.charges: Staging a seditious anti-colonial drama
cases.sentence: Arrested May 14, 1903 for staging Kahapon, Ngayon at Bukas; released on bail in December 1903, rearrested in June 1904, and eventually paroled on February 5, 1907.

name: Macario Sakay
description: Taken into custody after accepting a deceptive surrender invitation in approximately July 1906. He was held at Old Bilibid Prison in Manila and executed on September 13, 1907.

cases.charges: Armed anti-colonial resistance (Tagalog Republic)
cases.sentence: Taken into custody after a deceptive surrender in approximately July 1906, held at Old Bilibid Prison, and executed on September 13, 1907.

name: Lucio de Vega
description: Captured with Macario Sakay's movement and imprisoned at Old Bilibid Prison. He was executed together with Sakay on September 13, 1907.

cases.charges: Armed anti-colonial resistance (Tagalog Republic)
cases.sentence: Captured with Sakay's movement, imprisoned at Old Bilibid Prison, and executed together with Sakay on September 13, 1907.

name: Francisco Carreón
description: Captured around July 14, 1906 and imprisoned in Old Bilibid Prison. He was sentenced to life imprisonment on August 6, 1906, remained incarcerated long after 1910, and was pardoned in 1930.

cases.charges: Armed anti-colonial resistance (Tagalog Republic)
cases.sentence: Captured around July 14, 1906, imprisoned in Old Bilibid Prison, sentenced to life imprisonment on August 6, 1906, and pardoned in 1930 after remaining incarcerated long past 1910.

name: Julián Montalan
description: Captured during the suppression of the Sakay movement and reportedly received a life sentence rather than execution. Exact arrest and release documentation is less complete than for Sakay and Carreón.

cases.charges: Armed anti-colonial resistance (Tagalog Republic)
cases.sentence: Captured during the suppression of the Sakay movement and reportedly given a life sentence; exact arrest and release dates are less complete than for Sakay and Carreón, so release date is omitted.

name: Ricardo Flores Magón
description: A leader of the Partido Liberal Mexicano, Ricardo Flores Magón was arrested in Los Angeles on August 23, 1907. He was prosecuted and served roughly eighteen months in custody before being released around August 1910.

cases.charges: Arrest and prosecution as a PLM leader
cases.sentence: Arrested in Los Angeles on August 23, 1907, held and prosecuted for roughly eighteen months, and released around August 1910 (sources differ between August 1 and 3).

name: Librado Rivera
description: A prominent Partido Liberal Mexicano organizer, Librado Rivera was arrested in Los Angeles on August 23, 1907, and released around August 1910. He had earlier been arrested in 1906 in an unsuccessful extradition proceeding.

cases.charges: Arrest and prosecution as a PLM organizer
cases.sentence: Arrested in Los Angeles on August 23, 1907, and released around August 1910; he had also been arrested in 1906 in an unsuccessful extradition proceeding.

name: Antonio I. Villarreal
description: Antonio I. Villarreal, a Partido Liberal Mexicano leader, was arrested in Los Angeles on August 23, 1907. He was held for roughly three years before being released around August 1910.

cases.charges: Arrest and prosecution as a PLM leader
cases.sentence: Arrested in Los Angeles on August 23, 1907, held for roughly three years, and released around August 1910.

name: Lázaro Gutiérrez de Lara
description: Lázaro Gutiérrez de Lara was jailed beginning September 27, 1907, in California and released after 104 days, around January 1908. In October 1909 U.S. immigration officials seized him again as an alleged anarchist, though the duration of that detention is unclear.

cases.charges: Jailed as a PLM associate; later immigration detention
cases.sentence: Jailed from September 27, 1907, and released after 104 days around January 1908; in October 1909 immigration officials seized him again as an alleged anarchist for an unclear duration.

name: Manuel Sarabia
description: Manuel Sarabia, a Partido Liberal Mexicano militant, was seized on June 30, 1907, in Arizona and kidnapped across the border, held in the Hermosillo penitentiary about five days until public pressure secured his return. He was later arrested again in the United States as an editor of Revolución, released on bail, and fled abroad.

cases.charges: Cross-border kidnapping and later arrest as an editor of Revolución
cases.sentence: Seized on June 30, 1907, in Arizona and kidnapped across the border, held about five days in the Hermosillo penitentiary until public pressure secured his return; later arrested again in the U.S. as an editor of Revolución, released on bail, and fled abroad.

name: Antonio de Pío Araujo
description: Antonio de Pío Araujo was arrested on September 14, 1908, in Texas and imprisoned at the Leavenworth Federal Penitentiary in Kansas for violating U.S. neutrality laws. He remained imprisoned throughout 1910 and was released on February 9, 1911.

cases.charges: Violating U.S. neutrality laws
cases.sentence: Arrested September 14, 1908, in Texas, imprisoned at the Leavenworth Federal Penitentiary throughout 1910, and released on February 9, 1911.

name: Modesto Díaz
description: Modesto Díaz was jailed in a criminal-libel prosecution connected to the Partido Liberal Mexicano press. Contemporary accounts said his health was destroyed by the imprisonment and that he died following it; exact jail dates are uncertain.

cases.charges: Criminal-libel prosecution connected to the PLM press
cases.sentence: Jailed in a criminal-libel prosecution tied to the PLM press; contemporary accounts said his health was destroyed and that he died following his release, though exact jail dates are uncertain.

name: Federico Arizméndez
description: Federico Arizméndez was jailed in the Los Angeles criminal-libel campaign against the Partido Liberal Mexicano press. The exact dates of his imprisonment were not recovered and his release is not documented.

cases.charges: Los Angeles criminal-libel prosecution of the PLM press
cases.sentence: Jailed in the Los Angeles criminal-libel campaign against the PLM press; exact dates were not recovered and release not documented.

name: Ulibarri
description: Identified only by his surname in the contemporary account, Ulibarri was a young Partido Liberal Mexicano-associated defendant jailed in the same Los Angeles libel prosecution as Modesto Díaz and Federico Arizméndez. Exact dates are unknown and his release is not documented.

cases.charges: Los Angeles criminal-libel prosecution of the PLM press
cases.sentence: A young PLM-associated defendant jailed in the same Los Angeles libel prosecution as Díaz and Arizméndez; exact dates unknown and release not documented.

name: Enrique Flores Magón
description: Enrique Flores Magón was briefly jailed in San Antonio, Texas, around 1904 following a politically charged confrontation, and was later arrested in connection with the Partido Liberal Mexicano press. Exact dates are incomplete.

cases.charges: Jailed after a politically charged confrontation; later PLM press arrest
cases.sentence: Briefly jailed in San Antonio around 1904 after a politically charged confrontation and later arrested in connection with the PLM press; exact dates incomplete.

name: John Murray
description: John Murray, a United States socialist and supporter of the Partido Liberal Mexicano, was arrested by Secret Service agents for raising money for the Mexican prisoners' defense. He was later also prosecuted in a neutrality case; exact detention dates were not preserved.

cases.charges: Arrested for fundraising for the prisoners' defense; later neutrality prosecution
cases.sentence: Arrested by Secret Service agents for raising money for the Mexican prisoners' defense and later prosecuted in a neutrality case; exact detention dates were not preserved.

name: Lázaro Puente

name: Paul Corcoran
description: Paul Corcoran was a member of the Western Federation of Miners imprisoned in 1899 for a killing arising from the Coeur d'Alene labor conflict in Idaho. He was pardoned and released in August 1901 after roughly two years in custody. Supporters considered his conviction a frame-up.

cases.charges: Killing arising from Coeur d'Alene labor conflict
cases.sentence: Imprisoned for roughly two years before being pardoned and released; supporters considered the conviction a frame-up.

name: Charles H. Moyer
description: Charles H. Moyer, president of the Western Federation of Miners, was seized by the Colorado militia on March 30, 1904 and detained without an ordinary criminal complaint until mid-June 1904. In 1906 he was arrested and transported to Idaho with William Haywood for the murder prosecution of former governor Frank Steunenberg, and was held until the prosecution abandoned its case in January 1908.

cases.charges: Military detention without criminal complaint
cases.sentence: Detained by the Colorado militia without an ordinary criminal complaint until roughly June 15, 1904 (approximate).

cases.charges: Murder prosecution of former governor Frank Steunenberg (case abandoned)
cases.sentence: Held until the prosecution abandoned its case in January 1908.

name: William D. Haywood
description: William D. Haywood, a leader of the Western Federation of Miners, was arrested in Denver on February 17, 1906 and forcibly transported to Idaho for the murder prosecution of former governor Frank Steunenberg. He was acquitted on July 29, 1907 after roughly seventeen months in custody.

cases.charges: Murder prosecution of former governor Frank Steunenberg
cases.sentence: Acquitted on July 29, 1907 after roughly seventeen months in custody following forcible transport from Denver to Idaho.

name: George A. Pettibone
description: George A. Pettibone was arrested and transported with William Haywood and Charles Moyer in February 1906 for the Steunenberg murder prosecution in Idaho. He was imprisoned until his acquittal on January 4, 1908.

cases.charges: Murder prosecution of former governor Frank Steunenberg
cases.sentence: Imprisoned until acquittal on January 4, 1908 after being transported with Haywood and Moyer.

name: Steve Adams
description: Steve Adams was arrested in 1906 in connection with the Western Federation of Miners murder prosecutions in Idaho and held through a succession of murder trials and retrials. Three prosecutions against him failed, and he spent roughly three years in custody before regaining his freedom around 1909.

cases.charges: Murder prosecutions (three failed trials)
cases.sentence: Held through a succession of murder trials and retrials; three prosecutions failed and he spent roughly three years in custody before regaining freedom around 1909.

name: Annie Adams
description: Annie Adams was the wife of Steve Adams, confined with her children inside the Idaho penitentiary under the claim that they were held for protection. The confinement was used to pressure Steve Adams to testify.

cases.charges: Confined inside penitentiary to pressure husband to testify
cases.sentence: Confined with her children inside the Idaho penitentiary under the claim they were held for protection, to pressure Steve Adams to testify.

name: Vincent St. John
description: Vincent St. John, a Western Federation of Miners and Industrial Workers of the World leader, was jailed in May 1907 on a conspiracy-to-murder allegation. The charge was eventually dismissed.

cases.charges: Conspiracy to murder (dismissed)
cases.sentence: Jailed on a conspiracy-to-murder allegation that was eventually dismissed; exact release date not documented.

name: Morrie R. Preston
description: Morrie R. Preston, an Industrial Workers of the World member, was convicted in the politicized Goldfield murder case in 1907 and sentenced to 25 years. He was imprisoned throughout the decade and paroled in 1914.

cases.charges: Murder (Goldfield case)
cases.convicted: Yes — 25 years (Goldfield case; Nevada posthumously pardoned him in 1987)
cases.sentence: Sentenced to 25 years in the politicized Goldfield murder case and imprisoned throughout the decade before being paroled in 1914.

name: Joseph William Smith
description: Joseph William Smith, an Industrial Workers of the World member, was convicted with Morrie Preston in 1907 in the Goldfield case and sentenced to 10 years. He remained imprisoned throughout 1910.

cases.charges: Murder (Goldfield case)
cases.sentence: Sentenced to 10 years in the Goldfield case and remained imprisoned throughout 1910; source does not give his release date.

name: Jack Jones
description: Jack Jones was arrested on September 29, 1909 in the Missoula IWW street-speaking free-speech fight in Montana. The charges were abandoned and the prisoners released by October 8, 1909.

cases.charges: Street-speaking (free-speech fight)
cases.sentence: Charges abandoned and prisoners released by October 8, 1909 in the Missoula street-speaking fight.

name: Frank Little
description: Frank Little was arrested on September 29, 1909 in the Missoula IWW street-speaking free-speech fight in Montana. He was released by October 8, 1909.

cases.charges: Street-speaking (free-speech fight)
cases.sentence: Arrested in the Missoula street-speaking fight and released by October 8, 1909.

name: Elizabeth Gurley Flynn
description: Elizabeth Gurley Flynn was arrested on October 3, 1909 in the Missoula IWW free-speech fight and released by October 8, 1909. She was later jailed after participating in the Spokane street-speaking free-speech campaign in Washington, held until the remaining free-speech prisoners were released on March 4, 1910 following a March 3 settlement.

cases.charges: Street-speaking (free-speech fight)
cases.sentence: Arrested in the Missoula free-speech fight and released by October 8, 1909.

cases.charges: Street-speaking (free-speech fight)
cases.sentence: Jailed after participating in the Spokane street-speaking free-speech campaign; released with the remaining free-speech prisoners on March 4, 1910 after a March 3 settlement.

name: Edith Frenette
description: Edith Frenette was arrested on November 3, 1909 with roughly twenty men in the Spokane free-speech fight in Washington. The remaining prisoners were freed by March 4, 1910.

cases.charges: Street-speaking (free-speech fight)
cases.sentence: Arrested with roughly twenty men in the Spokane free-speech fight; remaining prisoners freed by March 4, 1910.

name: Sam T. Crane
description: Sam T. Crane was arrested on November 5, 1909 in the Spokane IWW free-speech fight in Washington. He was released on March 4, 1910.

cases.charges: Street-speaking (free-speech fight)
cases.sentence: Arrested in the Spokane fight and released on March 4, 1910.

name: E. Cousins
description: E. Cousins was identified among the arrested Spokane IWW leaders in November 1909 in Washington. He was released on March 4, 1910.

cases.charges: Street-speaking (free-speech fight)
cases.sentence: Identified among arrested Spokane IWW leaders in November 1909 and released on March 4, 1910.

name: C. L. Filigno
description: C. L. Filigno was arrested among the Spokane IWW leaders in November 1909 in Washington. He was released on March 4, 1910.

cases.charges: Street-speaking (free-speech fight)
cases.sentence: Arrested among Spokane IWW leaders in November 1909 and released on March 4, 1910.

name: James P. Wilson
description: James P. Wilson was arrested among the Spokane IWW leaders in November 1909 in Washington. He was released on March 4, 1910.

cases.charges: Street-speaking (free-speech fight)
cases.sentence: Arrested among Spokane IWW leaders in November 1909 and released on March 4, 1910.

name: E. J. Foote
description: E. J. Foote was arrested among the Spokane IWW leaders in November 1909 in Washington. He was released on March 4, 1910.

cases.charges: Street-speaking (free-speech fight)
cases.sentence: Arrested among Spokane IWW leaders in November 1909 and released on March 4, 1910.

name: James Doyle
description: James Doyle was jailed around December 1910 in the Fresno free-speech fight in California. He was released on January 26, 1911 after 51 days without trial.

cases.charges: Street-speaking (free-speech fight)
cases.sentence: Jailed in the Fresno free-speech fight and released on January 26, 1911 after 51 days without trial.

name: Leon Czolgosz
description: Leon Czolgosz, an anarchist, was arrested on September 6, 1901 for assassinating President William McKinley in New York. He was executed on October 29, 1901.

cases.charges: Assassination of President William McKinley
cases.sentence: Executed on October 29, 1901; Emma Goldman and other anarchists rejected claims of an organized conspiracy.

name: Clara Lemlich
description: Clara Lemlich was a labor organizer who helped spark the 1909-1910 New York shirtwaist strike, known as the Uprising of the 20,000. She was arrested roughly seventeen times for strike and picket-line activity during the walkout. Her militant call for a general strike galvanized thousands of garment workers.

cases.charges: Picketing during the 1909-1910 New York shirtwaist strike (Uprising of the 20,000)
cases.sentence: She was arrested about seventeen times for strike and picket-line activity, but the full arrest-and-release chronology is not recorded.

name: Alexander Berkman
description: Alexander Berkman was an anarchist imprisoned for the 1892 attempted assassination of industrialist Henry Clay Frick during the Homestead strike. He remained a political prisoner throughout the early 1900s, serving nearly fourteen years before his release. He later became a prominent anarchist writer and editor.

cases.charges: Attempted assassination of Henry Clay Frick
cases.sentence: He served nearly fourteen years in prison before his release on May 18, 1906.

name: Emma Goldman
description: Emma Goldman was a leading anarchist arrested on September 10, 1901 in the roundup following President McKinley's assassination. She was held for about two weeks on an unsupported conspiracy allegation. Authorities released her when they found no evidence connecting her to the crime.

cases.charges: Alleged conspiracy in the McKinley assassination (no evidence found)
cases.sentence: She was held for about two weeks and released when authorities found no evidence connecting her to the crime.

name: Abraham Isaak
description: Abraham Isaak was an anarchist publisher arrested and detained during the September 1901 roundup of anarchists following McKinley's assassination. He was released without prosecution when no evidence of conspiracy emerged.

cases.charges: Detained in the post-assassination anarchist roundup
cases.sentence: He was released without prosecution.

name: Mary Isaak
description: Mary Isaak was an anarchist arrested with Abe Isaak and other anarchists in September 1901 during the roundup following McKinley's assassination. She was released when no evidence of conspiracy emerged.

cases.charges: Detained in the post-assassination anarchist roundup
cases.sentence: She was released when no evidence of conspiracy emerged.

name: Hippolyte Havel
description: Hippolyte Havel was an anarchist held in the post-assassination anarchist roundup of September 1901. No prosecution followed his detention.

cases.charges: Detained in the post-assassination anarchist roundup
cases.sentence: No prosecution followed his detention.

name: Johann Most
description: Johann Most was an anarchist arrested after the McKinley assassination for republishing an article discussing tyrannicide. He was convicted of disturbing the public peace and given a one-year Blackwell's Island sentence beginning in 1901.

cases.charges: Republishing an article discussing tyrannicide
cases.sentence: He was given a one-year sentence at Blackwell's Island beginning in 1901.

name: John Turner
description: John Turner was a British anarchist arrested on October 23, 1903 under the Anarchist Exclusion Act. He was detained at Ellis Island for about three months before his release on $5,000 bail.

cases.charges: Detention under the Anarchist Exclusion Act
cases.sentence: He was detained at Ellis Island for about three months before release on $5,000 bail.

name: William MacQueen
description: William MacQueen was an anarchist editor arrested after the 1902 Paterson silk strike. He was convicted on a politically charged incitement allegation and sentenced to five years, serving about three years before release conditioned on leaving the United States.

cases.charges: Incitement after the 1902 Paterson silk strike
cases.sentence: He was sentenced to five years and served about three years before release conditioned on leaving the United States.

name: Rudolf Grossmann
description: Rudolf Grossmann was an anarchist arrested with William MacQueen and Luigi Galleani in connection with the 1902 Paterson silk strike. The precise time he spent in jail and the disposition of his case are not clearly established.

cases.charges: Detention in connection with the 1902 Paterson silk strike
cases.sentence: The precise time he spent in jail and the disposition of his case are not clearly established.

name: Luigi Galleani
description: Luigi Galleani was an anarchist charged after the 1902 Paterson silk strike but initially escaped arrest. He was captured on December 30, 1906 and jailed through his April 1907 trial. He was released after the jury failed to reach a verdict.

cases.charges: Incitement after the 1902 Paterson silk strike
cases.sentence: He was jailed through his April 1907 trial and released after the jury failed to reach a verdict.

name: Moses Harman
description: Moses Harman was a free-love and sex-education publisher imprisoned under the Comstock laws. He entered Joliet on March 1, 1906, was transferred to Leavenworth on June 28, 1906, and was released on December 26, 1906 after serving ten months and three days.

cases.charges: Obscenity under the Comstock laws
cases.sentence: He entered Joliet on March 1, 1906, was transferred to Leavenworth on June 28, 1906, and was released on December 26, 1906 after serving ten months and three days.

name: Ida Craddock
description: Ida Craddock was a free-speech advocate arrested on March 5, 1902 for distributing The Wedding Night. She was sentenced to three months and served most of the term at the Blackwell's Island workhouse, then was immediately rearrested under federal obscenity law. Facing a five-year federal sentence, she died by suicide on October 16, 1902 before that imprisonment began.

cases.charges: Distributing The Wedding Night
cases.sentence: She served most of a three-month term at the Blackwell's Island workhouse, then, facing a five-year federal sentence after rearrest, died by suicide on October 16, 1902 before the federal term began.

name: William Buwalda
description: William Buwalda was a U.S. Army private court-martialed after attending an Emma Goldman lecture on April 26, 1908 and shaking her hand while in uniform. He was sentenced initially to five years at hard labor, reduced to three years, and served about ten months at Alcatraz before a presidential pardon.

cases.charges: Court-martial for shaking Emma Goldman's hand in uniform
cases.sentence: He was sentenced initially to five years at hard labor, reduced to three years, and served about ten months at Alcatraz before a presidential pardon.

name: William Monroe Trotter
description: William Monroe Trotter was a civil-rights editor arrested after the July 30, 1903 Boston meeting where he challenged Booker T. Washington's accommodationist policies. He was convicted of disturbing the meeting and served 30 days at the Charles Street Jail.

cases.charges: Disturbing a public meeting
cases.sentence: He was convicted of disturbing the meeting and served 30 days.

name: Granville Martin
description: Granville Martin was arrested and convicted with William Monroe Trotter after the same July 30, 1903 Boston confrontation over Booker T. Washington's policies. He served about 30 days at the Charles Street Jail.

cases.charges: Disturbing a public meeting
cases.sentence: He was convicted with Trotter and served about 30 days.

name: Chitto Harjo
description: Chitto Harjo was a Muscogee (Creek) leader arrested on January 27, 1901 along with a large body of followers resisting the dissolution of Muscogee government and communal lands. The detention appears to have been comparatively brief, with sentences suspended and prisoners sent home.

cases.charges: Resisting the dissolution of Muscogee (Creek) government and communal lands
cases.sentence: The detention appears to have been comparatively brief, with sentences suspended and prisoners sent home.
